dev: Crusoe and Lancium, with Meta reported as the customer
power: 1 GW, grid connection already approved by ERCOT
water: Lancium told a Texas House committee it would draw about 11,000 gal/day from the Red River Water Authority and return 1 million gal/day; the companies promise closed-loop cooling
note: One campus: Lancium owns the 270 acres and the power hookup, and Crusoe builds the data centers. Announced July 2026 with Meta reported as the customer; by October two buildings were under construction. Two months after the announcement, the town was under a boil-water notice and a disaster declaration after extreme heat, and Lancium offered the city a possible new water source.
src: Crusoe and Lancium; Inside Climate News; TechRadar

name: IREN Childress AI and mining campus
power: About 750 MW operating, IREN's largest site
note: Started as a bitcoin mine in 2022. IREN has since added liquid-cooled AI halls, including capacity for Microsoft. Together with the Crusoe/Lancium campus, Childress would host close to 2 GW of data centers.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Geronimo Power AI data center
note: Ammannsville-Dubina area. Listed by the More Than Just Parks tracker; needs verification.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: PlaceMKR AI data center (Winchester)
note: Listed by the More Than Just Parks tracker; needs verification.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Project Caprock (Abernathy)
power: 540 MW, from Xcel Energy on the Southwest Power Pool grid, not ERCOT
note: Ground broken April 2026 on 313 acres just outside Abernathy: six buildings, about $5B. A separate campus from TeraWulf and Fluidstack, about 2 miles away.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: TeraWulf / Fluidstack Abernathy
dev: TeraWulf (51%) and Fluidstack (49%), with Google backing $1.3B of the lease
note: About 120 acres, due in the second half of 2026 under a 25-year lease. The companies describe the customer only as a developer of frontier AI models; one industry tracker names it as Anthropic. A separate campus from Aligned's Project Caprock.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: CloudBurst San Marcos Gigacenter
note: The same project as the Guadalupe County Technology Center card: CloudBurst's campus at 2955 Francis Harris Lane straddles the Hays-Guadalupe line. It sits outside San Marcos, which banned data centers inside city limits in June 2026. See the Guadalupe card for the full record.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Sabey / Carson Select San Marcos campus
dev: Sabey Data Centers, with landowner Carson Select Investments
note: About 786 acres south of San Marcos, the third data center proposed within 1.5 miles of the Hays Energy gas plant. The landowner told the city it had been "overwhelmed with unsolicited offers" before choosing Sabey. The council began negotiating in June 2025; we found no construction. The San Marcos River Foundation is tracking seven proposed data centers in the river's watershed.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Telios Quinlan Campus
note: 265 acres near Quinlan with an on-site substation; first power expected 2027.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Port Arthur AI data center
dev: Not yet confirmed in written records
note: Pitched to the Port Arthur City Council in Apr 2026 as a data center around Pleasure Island with its own wind, solar, battery storage and a small port. About 1.5 miles from protected public land, per the tracker. Needs a written record.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: FluidStack Cameron County campus
water: Company promises closed-loop cooling; water from the East Rio Hondo Water Supply Corporation
note: More than 1,100 acres along FM 106 near Rio Hondo. After Harlingen tabled the company's drainage request following public pushback, the project went ahead in unincorporated county land, where the county says it has little zoning power. Site work began in September 2026 on a county worksite permit. Harlingen now has a moratorium on new data center applications.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Wichita Falls Business Park data center
dev: Skybox Datacenters, through Texas Data Centers Campus LLC
power: Skybox markets 300+ MW; the tracker lists 800 MW
note: Six to 10 buildings; Skybox says 300 to 500 permanent jobs and 2,000 to 3,000 construction workers. Groundbreaking pushed to early 2027 after the state audit.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Bells AI data center
dev: Black Mountain (CEO Rhett Bennett confirmed it was exploring the site)
power: Size not disclosed; a power plant permit was filed by a company at Black Mountain's address
note: Neighbors found it themselves, through survey markers, land records and a permit search, before any public announcement. Same developer as Black Mountain's Fort Worth and Dinosaur Valley projects.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Delta County data center
dev: LS Power (per the tracker; not yet confirmed in local reporting)
note: County Judge Tanner Crutcher said the project was not a good fit, with water his main worry, and residents raised water contracts tied to Cooper Lake. Commissioners voted in March 2026 to oppose tax abatements for data centers. The developer's name has not appeared in local reporting.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: CyrusOne Jack County campus
water: Company says closed-loop cooling with a one-time fill of 200,000 gallons; Wise County residents questioned that figure
note: A $600M first phase beside Vistra's gas plant on Hwy 199 at the Wise County line. The crowd was big enough that the county moved its hearing to the district courtroom, and neighboring Wise County asked the state for a special session on data centers. This is CyrusOne's pattern in Texas: Freestone, Bosque, Jack, and now Sulphur Springs all pair a data center with a gas plant.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Prometheus Hyperscale Kaufman campus
dev: Prometheus Hyperscale, with Engie North America
power: 200 MW in four 50 MW buildings; listed with on-site gas generation and batteries
note: About 500 acres between Talty and Post Oak Bend City, a few miles from Flexential's Talty campus. The same company plans up to 2.5 GW in Reeves County.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Crusoe Jayton campus
power: Size not disclosed; two buildings of about 759,000 sq ft each
note: A $4.8B campus filed with the state in October 2026, in a county of fewer than 1,000 people. Kent County noticed a tax abatement hearing in August. Construction is set for January 2027. It sits between Crusoe's Abilene and Childress builds, with another Crusoe complex proposed next door in Stonewall County.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Kahla Project (Marquez)
dev: Crusoe Technologies (first proposed by Belltown Power)
note: A $34B campus near Marquez, between Centerville and Bremond. After 200+ residents packed the room, Leon County commissioners rejected Crusoe's initial tax break application. Residents organized fast, including a local podcast; two more data centers are proposed in the county.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: LAMP power and innovation hub
power: 240 MW gas plant being built on site; studying up to 1 GW of nuclear microreactors; the tracker lists 3 GW
water: Company says it will not rely only on local aquifers; amount not disclosed
note: 701 acres near Raywood. The county says it was told about a plastics plant for PPE and learned of the data center from a newspaper. The company calls itself an accidental data center builder.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Cipher Mikeska HPC data center
note: About 100 acres outside Brady, first bought as a bitcoin mining site. One of three Cipher option sites in Texas marketed at 500 MW each (with Milsing and McLennan); Cipher also plans Colchis near San Angelo. Power was promised for 2027; trackers now say 2028 to 2030. Pin is approximate.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Cipher Milsing HPC data center
note: About 187 acres outside Huntsville, first bought for bitcoin mining. Cipher lists it for 2030 or later, behind its Tom Green, McLennan and McCulloch sites.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Crusoe Victoria AI Factory
dev: Crusoe, with Blue Energy and GE Vernova
power: 1 GW of gas turbines first, then up to 1.5 GW from five small nuclear reactors
note: A 1,600-acre campus at the Port of Victoria. The power timeline has already slipped: gas was promised for 2028 and nuclear for 2031; the revised plan says gas in 2030 and reactors from 2032.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Data City Texas
power: Claims 5 GW, starting with 300 MW, all behind the meter
water: Not disclosed, in a county where colonias already face water insecurity
note: Announced in 2025 as the world's largest behind-the-meter data center hub, on 50,000 acres near Laredo. As of 2026, the city and county say no application has been filed. Laredo is writing permanent data center rules.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Desert Haven data center
dev: ServerDomes Global with Kaufman & Company (Lonestar Kaufman Development Partners)
power: 350 MW, mostly from its own on-site power; Rio Grande Electric Co-op serves the area
note: Hueco Ranch: a $15B campus of geodesic domes on about 24,000 acres. Ground was broken Oct 7, 2026 before neighbors or county officials were told; the CEO later apologized. Residents have formed a group.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Project Eagle (AWS)
note: A $10B campus on about 3,000 acres near Boling, a town of under 400. Ten buildings filed with the state in 2026. County officials signed an NDA with Amazon's consultant, which limits what the public is told. Could become the largest data center campus in Texas.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Project Roman (Hereford)
power: Size not disclosed; a related 500 MW solar project is planned for 2028
water: Not disclosed, over the Ogallala Aquifer, where Hereford's water plan warns of shortages
note: Planned north of Hereford (map pin is the town, not the site). Hundreds packed the civic center for answers. The hospital district board took up Google's tax break while saying it would not consider water or environmental impact.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Google Wilbarger County data center
dev: Google, with AES building power on site
power: Size not disclosed by Google; one tracker lists 850 MW
water: Air-cooled; Google says the design aims to eliminate operational water use
note: Two buildings of about 991,000 sq ft each near Vernon, about $1B, with work begun March 2026. Google is giving the city $4.5M for infrastructure. Worth noting: if Google can air-cool here, other developers can be asked to do the same.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Project North (Shackelford)
dev: Bolt Data and Energy (backed in part by Texas Pacific Land)
note: A second campus proposed west of Albany, in a county already hosting Vantage's $25B Frontier site. Residents asked, "Do we need another one?" and the county judge held one-on-one meetings after the backlash. Pin is approximate.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: BlockchAIn Wise County mining site
note: A bitcoin mining site the company lists in its investor pipeline as in due diligence, with power targeted for late 2026. Wise County officials said in 2026 that no data center project had approached the county. Exact site not published.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Ziastra (Marfa)
dev: Open Origin (an ammonia and green fuels company)
power: Planned to be all on-site solar, off the grid
water: The company advertises zero water for cooling, but a county official said it plans to pump 800 acre-feet of groundwater a year, about 714,000 gallons a day, more than the City of Marfa uses
note: Proposed on about 80,000 acres of ranchland southeast of Marfa. The company promised 900 to 1,100 jobs; none were posted. It said its supercomputer would go live in early 2025.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Matrix Data Center Campus (Sulphur Springs)
dev: Was MSB Global; CyrusOne now considering it
power: MSB planned 3 GW in 30 buildings; CyrusOne pitches an on-site gas plant
water: CyrusOne says about 1,000 gal/day per building
note: On a coal mine site Luminant gave the city. The old owner says the deed bars power generation, a judge has barred it until a 2027 trial, and construction stopped. Council minutes never mentioned the project. MSB is out; CyrusOne held a community meeting in Sept 2026.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Project Aggie
dev: Priority Power Management (PPM Data LLC), backed by I Squared Capital
power: 600 MW planned, with two 300 MW substations
note: Planned on about 200 acres of city land in College Station's Midtown Business Park. Amid strong opposition, the City Council refused to sell the land, which stopped the project there.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Zydeco Hutto data center
note: Stopped by residents. Zydeco needed land zoned for apartments rezoned to heavy industrial. City staff recommended denial, and the Stop the Hutto Data Center group filed formal written protests that would have forced a three-fourths council vote. Zydeco withdrew in April 2026, days before the P&Z hearing.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Data Factory Athens
power: 10 MW to start, with bitcoin mining
note: After a packed council meeting, Athens paused data centers, then voted 3 to 2 in Aug 2026 for an ordinance banning them. A win for residents, near the separate Diode project at Cedar Creek Lake that was also withdrawn.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: NFN8 Crystal City bitcoin mine
note: A bitcoin mine in a leased warehouse on Old Uvalde Highway. A fire at the site around the 2025 holidays cut the company's capacity in half, and NFN8 filed for bankruptcy in February 2026 and is selling its assets. A reminder to ask any developer: who pays to clean up if the company goes under?
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Airport Drive data center
dev: Applicant Brad Altman; data center operator never identified
note: Rejected. The applicant asked to rezone land zoned for apartments, beside existing homes, to light industrial. The council worried the rezoning would allow other industrial uses too, and voted unanimously no in May 2026, citing the homes and the unknown developer. Three months later the city approved a much smaller data center next door that reuses an empty grocery store building, with conditions.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Highlander SM One (San Marcos)
note: This is the same project as the San Marcos data center on Francis Harris Lane, which the City Council denied in Feb 2026. See that card for the full record.
src: More Than Just Parks data center tracker

name: Sabey Oklaunion
note: Land Sabey is holding for a future campus near Oklaunion, a few miles from Google's Vernon campus and an operating bitcoin mine. The same developer behind the San Marcos and Round Rock projects. Pin is approximate.
src: Data Center Dynamics; Baxtel

name: GDA Rowdy (Vernon)
note: A bitcoin mine operating near Vernon since 2024, fed by the Oklaunion substation. With Google's campus and Sabey's planned site nearby, Wilbarger County now has three. Pin is approximate.
src: Bitcoin Magazine; Baxtel

name: Calvano data center (Wichita Falls)
note: Rezoning approved by the Wichita Falls City Council for a single-tenant hyperscale building of up to 2.3 million sq ft, placed beside an Oncor facility on purpose. The tenant has not been named. Pin is approximate.
src: Data Center Dynamics

name: DataNovaX (Airport Drive)
note: A small data center reusing an empty grocery store and call center building, approved with conditions in August 2026. Right next to the Airport Drive site the city rejected three months earlier: a contrast worth noting.
src: KAUZ
